title: They Couldn't Stop
narrativeQuestion: Can fear spread from one mind to the next like a disease?

chapters.title: The summer the city danced
chapters.claim: In 1518 Strasbourg's cure of stages and musicians spread a dancing outbreak that faded after a shrine pilgrimage. Mass psychogenic illness fits the clues better than ergot.

chapters.title: The gas that was never there
chapters.claim: In September 1944 the Mattoon Journal-Gazette headlines tracked the rise and fall of nearly thirty gas reports with no gas found.

chapters.title: The school that could not stop laughing
chapters.claim: Beginning January 30, 1962, 95 of 159 girls at Kashasha were affected, and closing the school carried it to villages.

chapters.title: The first outbreak spread by screen
chapters.claim: From 2019 to 2021 functional tic-like behavior spread through social media; Müller-Vahl's team named mass social media induced illness in 2021.

chapters.title: The case that is still open
chapters.claim: Havana Syndrome remains unresolved; the June 12, 2026 rescission of the 2023 and 2025 assessments reopened the question.

chapters.title: Climb out
chapters.claim: Students explain spread, leadership, the difference from faking, and what evidence would change their minds.

accuracyNotes: Strasbourg numbers given as the 50 to 400 range; later death counts flagged as unsupported.
The contagion engine is a model, not data; the real Kashasha figure is printed beside it.
Havana status stated as of November 2026.
